interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 2, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Cantaloupes in Todd's salad" e "Cantaloupes in Caroline's salad"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Charlie should eat the salad made by Todd."; "Charlie should eat the salad made by Caroline."; "Charlie will like both salads."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

campo numérico do denominador da segunda reta + confirmar
segunda reta numérica; o aluno marca o ponto da segunda fração
seletor com as alternativas de comparação; o aluno escolhe uma delas

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the size of the parts on the number line?
Look at the bottom number in Todd's fraction and enter that number in the division field.
Todd's fraction has a numerator on top and a denominator on the bottom; use the bottom number for the equal partitions.
Enter the denominator from Todd's fraction as the number of equal parts, then confirm the division.
How does the numerator tell you how many equal intervals to count from zero?
Count equal sixths from zero, passing the first whole when the numerator is greater than the denominator.
Todd's numerator tells you how many sixth-sized intervals to move along the number line.
Starting at zero, move eleven equal intervals of size one-sixth and place the marker at that position.
What does the denominator represent when a whole is divided on a number line?
Find the bottom number in Caroline's fraction and enter it as the number of equal parts.
Use the denominator, not the numerator, to determine the partition of Caroline's number line.
Enter Caroline's denominator as the number of equal intervals, then confirm the division.
How do the numerator and denominator work together to locate a fraction?
Count intervals whose size is one-fifth, using Caroline's numerator to determine how many intervals to move.
The denominator gives the interval size, while the numerator gives the number of intervals counted from zero.
Starting at zero, move ten equal intervals of size one-fifth and place the marker there.
On a number line, which quantity is greater: the point farther left or the point farther right?
Compare the locations of the two marked points rather than comparing only their numerators.
Look closely at which salad's marked point lies farther to the right on the number line from zero to two.
Select the salad connected to the point farther right, because that point represents the greater amount of cantaloupe.
What should you verify before completing a comparison on two number lines?
Check that both denominators were entered, both fraction positions were marked, and the comparison was selected.
Make sure the selected salad matches the point that is farther to the right.

Charlie is trying out the fruit salad that Todd and Caroline each made for the school picnic. Todd and Caroline used different recipes. Charlie wants to eat a salad with more cantaloupe.  Use the number line to find out whose salad Charlie should try.
Todd has cut up 11/6 cantaloupes.
Caroline has cut up 10/5 cantaloupes.
Which Salad should Charlie eat?
